newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up about 1/2 point on day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up about 1/2 point on day.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds climbed around half a point in late trade on Thursday, but whether the rise would be fully sustained was quickly called into question even though Treasuries soared, and looked likely to firm more.

"If Treasuries had not moved the way they did, I think we were just on the edge of having to move back a little. We're pushing the envelope and I think the next couple of days will show whether what we've done is real," said a municipal analyst. He pointed to near-record low ratios between the yield offered by municipals and Treasuries, which suggested the former might be overpriced.
However, that might prove to be the contrarian view.

Cash Treasury bonds looked set to see whether they could add to their gains, pushing down through the key 6.75 percent yield, as opinions strengthened that the Federal Reserve will leave rates unchanged at its next policy-making meeting in early July. And some of that strength could keep spilling over into the municipal market, as it did Thursday.
Further, even though this was expected to be the biggest week so far this year for new offerings, with next week's schedule also seen as large, redemptions are producing lots of cash for purchases.
MuniView said it anticipated redemptions in June to add up to over $35 billion, a level that should be surpassed in July, which could total more than $37 billion.
At present, most buying interest was clustered around intermediates in the municipal market.
"Your high-grade market was probably up an 0.03, but the long-end was probably up close to an 0.05...The market showed most of its improvement from 12 to 13 years out," the municipal analyst said.
In the secondary market, Dade County, Fla., Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.56 percent, NET, unchanged.
And Chicago, Ill., Board of Education Chicago School Reform of 2027, which have a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 100-1/2, up half a point.
The optimism over the central bank's likely stance was prompted by a surprising slip in U.S. retail sales. For the third month in a row, they fell, easing 0.1 percent in May.
The drop confounded economists polled by Reuters, who had expected a 0.4 percent increase.

Nor was that the only positive feature for fixed-income markets, which started firming early after the U.S. Labor Department surprised the market by reporting weekly jobless claims rose to 339,000 for the week ended June 7.
Analysts had expected claims to drop to 326,000 after a surge to 337,000 in the prior week.
In debt futures, the September municipal contracts ended up 28 ticks at 117-16/32, while September Treasury bond futures gained 25 ticks to 111-12/32. The MOB spread was 196 ticks, slightly firmer.
